chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isḥāq ibn Jarīr, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The prayer is complete in four places: in the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Ḥarām), and the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and the Mosque of Kufa, and the Sanctuary of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), may the prayers of Allah be upon him.'

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Messenger (Prophet Muhammad SAWW)

ai.seo_question: What are the four places where prayer is considered complete according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates four specific sanctuaries where the prayer is considered fully complete, elevating the status of the shrine of Imam al-Husayn alongside the three primary Islamic mosques. This inclusion underscores the unique spiritual hierarchy in Shia tradition, linking the legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt directly to the validity and perfection of ritual worship. It reflects the scholarly view that these sites serve as focal points for divine connection, reinforcing the theological importance of the Imams' resting places.
